title: State of Bilateral Relationship with Malaysia After Last Election
what_it_is: State of Bilateral Relationship with Malaysia After Last Election

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia bilateral relationship
sections.summary: A question asks about the state of Singapore's bilateral relationship with Malaysia and how collaboration will continue after Malaysia's GE14 changed its ruling coalition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs what is the state of our bilateral relationship with Malaysia and how will Singapore continue a collaborative and mutually beneficial relationship between the two countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Following Malaysia's 14th General Election (GE14) on 9 May 2018, the country's ruling coalition changed.

sections.label: Malaysian government issues raised
sections.summary: The passage notes a welcome for Foreign Minister Saifuddin Abdullah and reports on 1MDB investigations, possible HSR cancellation, and water price revision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I look forward to welcoming my counterpart Foreign Minister Saifuddin Abdullah at the end of this month for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Ministerial Meetings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But Members may have heard or read various reports on the new Malaysian government’s investigations into the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB)-linked financial flows, Members may have heard of their intentions to cancel or postpone the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail (HSR) Project, and some Members would also have heard – in fact, I think all of us would have heard – of their expressions to revise the price of water sold to Singapore under the 1962 Water Agreement.

sections.label: Malaysia discontinues ICJ applications
sections.summary: Singapore was prepared to argue its case at the ICJ, but the new Malaysian government requested to discontinue its applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We were fully prepared to argue our case at the ICJ.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: However, the new Malaysian government requested to discontinue their applications to the ICJ.

sections.label: Action against 1MDB breaches
sections.summary: Singapore took firm action against institutions and individuals breaking its laws, shutting two banks, levying fines, and jailing and fining convicted individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have taken firm action against both institutions and individuals who have broken our laws, including pursuing criminal prosecutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have shut down two banks and levied fines on other banks for regulatory breaches, and we have jailed and fined individuals who have been convicted on 1MDB-related charges.

sections.label: 1MDB information exchanges with Malaysia
sections.summary: Singapore provided 1MDB-related information in over 30 exchanges with Malaysia during the period, as Malaysia acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In total, we provided 1MDB-related information in over 30 exchanges with Malaysia during the period, as was, indeed, acknowledged by Malaysia.

sections.label: Assistance and legal processes for Malaysia
sections.summary: Singapore will continue assisting Malaysia's investigations and informed Malaysia it can use Singapore's Courts to establish ownership and recover seized 1MDB-linked assets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will continue to assist the Malaysian government in its own investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have also informed the Malaysian government that it can avail itself of due legal processes through our Courts to establish ownership and recover any assets seized in Singapore that can be traced to 1MDB.

sections.label: Compensation if Malaysia terminates HSR
sections.summary: If Malaysia terminates the HSR project, Singapore will seek compensation for costs incurred under the bilateral agreement and international law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Should Malaysia cause the HSR project to be terminated, we will deal with the question of compensation from Malaysia for costs incurred in accordance with the bilateral agreement and with international law.

sections.label: Malaysia lost water price review
sections.summary: Malaysia lost its right to review the price of water under the 1962 Water Agreement in 1987.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Malaysia lost its right to review the price of water under the 1962 Water Agreement in 1987.

sections.label: Johor buys treated water price
sections.summary: Johor currently buys treated water from Singapore at 50 Malaysian sen per 1,000 gallons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Johor currently buys treated water from Singapore at 50 Malaysian sen per 1,000 gallons.

sections.label: Linggiu Dam agreement and payments
sections.summary: In 1990 PUB and Johor agreed to build the Linggiu Dam; Singapore paid for it and paid Johor RM320 million, and disputes must be resolved peacefully under international law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In 1990, PUB and Johor signed an agreement to construct the Linggiu Dam to increase the yield of the Johor River in order to enable reliable abstraction of PUB's full entitlement of 250 million gallons (mgd) of water per day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Johor owns the Linggiu Dam, but Singapore paid for its construction and continues to pay for its operation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: These sums incurred are on top of the RM320 million – S$208 million at 1990 rates – that we paid to Johor in 1990, as compensation for the land used for the Linggiu Reservoir project and for the potential loss of revenue from logging activities, and as a one-time payment for the lease of that land for the remaining tenure of the 1962 Water Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are committed to engaging and cooperating with the new Malaysian government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But we must work with each other on the basis that both sides will fully respect the sanctity of international agreements, and that any disputes will be resolved peacefully in accordance with international law.
